scope: Historic demolished Bristol Hotel ensemble in Mar del Plata: original1888Tudor lodging house with attached lodging wings, distinct Italianate public/dining-salon building with its veranda/terrace/roof pavilions and the separate academicist guest annex on third block. Include characteristic timber-grid/gabled main house/slate roofs/turrets, masonry ground arches, balconies and thin intrinsic porch structures; distinct U-shaped public halls/own enclosed glazed terrace and corner pavilions; separate mansard-roofed annex with corner/central pavilions. Retain open inter-building/street gaps rather than merging blocks into a solid parcel. No modern Bristol Center replacement, surrounding streets/plaza/beach/landscape/city, hotels of the same name, tunnel interiors, people/vehicles/signs/flags/scenery. Surviving modern street intersections register an explicit historical reconstruction, not surveyed demolished building outlines. Complete representative1913three-block ensemble with explicitly estimated secondary lodging wings and guest-annex exterior; photographically established original/public forms retained.
